arms.description: Choose the most important personal value and write about why it matters to the participant before the self-focused cancer-risk passage
Choose the least important personal value and write only about why it could matter to another person before the same self-focused cancer-risk passage

omitted_source_cells.description: Active control with close-other-focused cancer-risk context

arm_subset_rule: Among the two source-randomized affirmation contrasts that hold target context fixed, retain lexicographically smaller source cells 1 and 3 under the frozen arm-subset rule.
outcome_question: I intend to lose weight in the next 6 months.
decision_maker: a health-risk communicator deciding whether to precede a self-focused cancer-risk message with the source self-affirmation exercise or its active writing control
beneficiary: the overweight adult receiving the self-focused health-risk message
utility_rationale: The source restricts the sample to adults with BMI 25 through 55, and the common passage identifies overweight or obesity as a cancer-risk factor. Higher Q9a values therefore represent stronger intention to pursue the source-targeted health behavior. This is a behavioral-intention utility, not verified weight loss or clinical benefit.
target_population: Adults aged 40 to 70 with source-screened BMI from 25 through 55, no reported cancer or skin-cancer diagnosis, and an eligible close relationship; the retained self-target contrast does not use the close-other outcome route.

interactive_treatment_contract.procedure: Arm-local value selection and writing occurs before the common self-focused cancer-risk passage and Q9a.

reconstruction_note: The final questionnaire alone freezes source cells 1 and 3, the complete interactive procedure, both sex-routed cancer passages, and Q9a bounds and orientation. No participant member, response value, aggregate, report, proposal, or result text was opened.
